379.name: Licensed Weed Control
379.body:
Weeds on the Western Slope are relentless. Long, dry summers and disturbed soils give hardy natives and noxious invaders every advantage, and once they set seed they come back worse the next year. Licensed weed control is about staying ahead of that cycle instead of chasing it.

Our applicators are licensed through the Colorado Department of Agriculture and are Colorado Certified Master Gardeners, so they know the weeds that actually grow here — from bindweed and puncturevine to the noxious species the county wants controlled. We match the product and timing to the weed and the season, treat lawns and landscape beds on a schedule, and set honest expectations: complete eradication is not realistic, but steady season-long management absolutely is.

Ask us about pairing weed control with an early-spring pre-emergent — stopping seeds before they sprout is the cheapest weed control there is.

383.name: Retaining Walls
383.body:
Our valleys are anything but flat. Terraced lots, sloping yards, and cut banks run from the Grand Mesa down to the river bottoms, and a retaining wall is often the difference between usable ground and a hillside you fight with a mower.

We build retaining walls that do their real job — holding back soil and water — as well as looking good doing it. That starts below the surface: proper base preparation, drainage behind the wall so runoff and freeze-thaw don't push it out, and materials sized to the load. A wall that isn't drained and built for our winters will lean and fail; one that is will outlast the house.

From a low garden wall to a structural, multi-tier system, we'll walk the site, talk through what the ground is doing, and build accordingly.

385.name: Rock Work
385.body:
Rock belongs in a high-desert landscape. It fits the country we live in, it doesn't ask for water, and it shrugs off sun, wind, and freeze-thaw — which is exactly why it's one of the most practical ways to add structure and character to a Western Slope yard.

We work with boulders, cobble, flagstone, and decorative rock to build dry creek beds that handle runoff, accent placements, borders, and full rock groundcover that ends the mowing and watering on the areas you'd rather not fuss with. Done right, rock work looks like it was always there.

Tell us what you're picturing — a single statement boulder or a whole low-water redesign — and we'll help you choose material that suits your site and your budget.

386.name: Sodding
386.body:
When you want a lawn now instead of next season, sod is the answer. It's the fastest way to go from bare dirt to established, usable turf — no waiting out germination, no washouts on a slope, no dust.

The real results are made under the sod. We prep the soil first — grading, amending our tight alkaline ground, and getting the base right — because sod laid on poor soil never roots the way it should. Laid on properly prepared ground and watered in correctly, it knits down fast and holds.

We'll help you pick a turf suited to our climate and your water situation, install it clean, and tell you exactly how to water it through those critical first weeks.

387.name: And More
387.body:
The list above covers most of what we do, but not all of it. After more than thirty years working outdoor spaces across Delta and Montrose counties, we've taken on just about every kind of project the Western Slope can hand a property.

If you've got something in mind that doesn't fit neatly into one of our service categories, ask. Chances are we've done something like it — and if we haven't, we'll tell you straight.

390.name: Misc Services
390.body:
Not every job fits a category. Over the years we've handled the one-off and the unusual — the projects that come up once and don't have a tidy name.

If you've got an outdoor project on your Delta or Montrose property and you're not sure who does that kind of work, start with us. We'll tell you honestly whether it's in our wheelhouse, and point you the right direction if it isn't.

396.name: Holiday Decorations
396.body:
The holidays are more fun when you're not the one on a ladder in the cold. We design, hang, and manage Christmas lighting and holiday décor so your home shows well all season — then take it all down and store it when the season's over.

Because we install professional-grade lighting the right way — clean runs, weatherproof connections, fixtures secured to take our wind and snow — the display holds up through a Western Slope winter instead of half-going-dark by New Year's.

Get on the schedule early; the calendar for holiday installs fills up well before Thanksgiving.

398.name: Licensed Insect Control
398.body:
The same trees and shrubs that make a Western Slope yard worth having are under steady pressure from insects — ips beetle in the pinyons, scale on the pines, borers in stressed deciduous trees, grubs in the lawn. Left alone, a small infestation becomes a dead tree.

Our technicians are licensed through the Colorado Department of Agriculture and trained in the pests that actually show up here. We identify the problem, treat it with the right product at the right time — timing is everything with insects — and, where prevention is the better play, get ahead of the pest before it does damage.

If something on your property looks stressed, off-color, or is dropping needles or leaves out of season, have us look before it spreads.

405.name: Trunk Bore Prevention
405.body:
Boring insects are among the few pests that can kill an otherwise healthy tree, and by the time the damage shows — sawdust at the base, dead branches, a thinning crown — the borers are already established under the bark. The only reliable defense is prevention.

We apply preventative trunk treatments timed to the pest and the season, putting a barrier in place before boring insects can get in. It's the cheapest insurance there is against losing a mature tree that took decades to grow and can't be replaced in a season.

Trees under water stress are the most vulnerable, so we'll also talk through watering — a well-hydrated tree defends itself far better than a dry one.

411.name: Spring Cleanup
411.body:
Spring cleanup is the reset that sets up your whole season. Winter leaves a yard full of matted debris, broken branches, gravel thrown by the plow, and the first flush of weeds — and the sooner that's cleared, the better everything grows once it warms up.

We rake out the turf, clear and edge the beds, cut back the perennials and grasses we left standing over winter for protection, haul off the debris, and get the property ready for the growing season. It's also the right time to see what came through the winter and what didn't.

Pair it with a spring sprinkler start-up and a pre-emergent, and your yard starts the year ahead instead of behind.

412.name: Summer Pruning
412.body:
Not all pruning waits for winter. Summer pruning, done while trees and shrubs are in active growth, is the right tool for shaping, thinning, and controlling size — the cuts heal quickly, and you can see exactly what you're doing with the plant in full leaf.

We use summer pruning to open crowded canopies for light and airflow (which helps hold down disease in our climate), keep hedges and ornamentals in bounds, and clean up structure without the hard, growth-forcing cuts that belong in the dormant season.

Heavy structural work still waits for winter — but for shaping and maintenance through the season, summer is the time.

414.name: Landscape Beds
414.body:
Landscape beds are where weeds go to hide — coming up through mulch, along edging, and in tight against the plants you're trying to protect. Spraying beds takes a more careful hand than spraying open lawn.

Our licensed applicators treat bed areas with products and techniques chosen to knock down weeds without harming your desirable plantings, timed to our growing season for the best result. Where spraying tight against valued plants isn't the right call, we'll say so and hand-pull instead.

Kept up on a schedule, treated beds stay clean and sharp instead of slowly disappearing under weeds by mid-summer.

415.name: Misc. Areas
415.body:
Some weed problems aren't in the lawn or the beds — they're in the gravel drive, the fence line, the alley, the vacant corner of the lot, or the ground around outbuildings. These odd areas are often where the worst weeds get a foothold and set seed for everything else.

We spray these problem areas with the right product for the setting — including bare-ground treatments where you want nothing to grow at all — handled by licensed applicators who know what's safe to use where.

Staying on top of the odd corners is how you keep them from re-seeding the areas you actually care about.

416.name: Weed Pulling in Shrubs
416.body:
Sometimes the right tool for weeds in a shrub bed is a pair of hands, not a sprayer. In tight against valued plantings — or for customers who'd rather keep spray to a minimum — hand-pulling clears the weeds with no risk to what you want to keep.

We pull weeds out of shrub and landscape beds, clean up along edging and hardscape, and leave the bed looking sharp. It's straightforward work, but on the Western Slope it's never one-and-done — bindweed and other persistent weeds come back, so the beds that stay clean are the ones kept up on a schedule.

417.name: Trees and Shrubs (Fertilizing)
417.body:
In a forest, trees feed themselves off the humus of the forest floor. In a yard — planted in our compacted, alkaline, limestone-heavy soil, competing with turf, and stressed by heat and drought — that natural feeding isn't there. Fertilizing puts it back.

We apply a slow-release granular fertilizer to your trees and shrubs in the spring, formulated for the nutrients our high-pH soils tend to lock away. It releases over roughly three to four months, feeding plants through the part of the season when they're growing most — and a well-fed tree or shrub is far more resistant to the insects and disease that pick off stressed plants.

It's one of the simplest, highest-return things you can do for the long-lived plants in your landscape.

378.name: Water Features
378.body:
There's something about moving water in a dry country, and a Western Slope yard is made for it. A pond, a waterfall, or a quiet bubbling stream becomes the place everyone gathers — and, built right, it does it without becoming a chore or a water hog.

We design and build water features that fit the landscape and run efficiently, with the pumps, liners, and circulation sized so the system does the work instead of you. The goal is a feature that looks like it belongs and holds up to our seasons, freeze and all.

Whether you're picturing a small courtyard fountain or a full backyard stream and pond, we'll help you plan something that fits your space, your budget, and how much upkeep you actually want.

382.name: Xeriscaping
382.body:
Xeriscaping isn't rock and cactus — it's smart landscaping for a place that doesn't get much rain. On the Western Slope, where water is expensive and summers are long and dry, a well-designed low-water landscape stays green and interesting on a fraction of what a traditional lawn demands.

We design and install xeriscapes around drought-tough plants that actually belong in our climate, grouped by water need, set in properly prepared soil, and backed by efficient drip irrigation and mulch or rock to hold what moisture there is. Done well, it isn't a compromise — it's a landscape that looks good and costs less to keep every year.

If your water bill climbs every summer, this is the conversation to have.

1277.name: Weed Control (Weed Spraying)
1277.body:
Weed spraying is the hands-on service behind the results — the actual applications our crews carry out across lawns, landscape beds, and problem areas through the growing season.

Our spray technicians are licensed through the Colorado Department of Agriculture and are Colorado Certified Master Gardeners, so they know our native and noxious weeds and match the product and timing to the target. We treat on a schedule, because weed control on the Western Slope is never one-and-done — our long dry summers and tough soils keep the pressure on all season.

Complete eradication isn't a realistic promise from anyone, but steady, licensed management that keeps weeds down and your landscape looking cared-for absolutely is.
